newsitem.title: UK: UK's Halifax sees big insurance, savings boom.
newsitem.headline: UK's Halifax sees big insurance, savings boom.

text.p: The Halifax Building Society, which on Friday announced details of a stock market flotation worth up to 12 billion stg, said it sees room for huge expansion in the UK insurance and long-term savings sectors.
"We'll focus on the UK personal financial services sector," Halifax spokesman Davis Gilchrist told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"That's a very wide area, both on the borrowing side and, increasingly, on the savings side -- traditional savings and long-term savings."
Gilchrist said this was a major growth area, with an ageing population in a declining welfare state.'
Asked whether the expansion would be by acquisition or through organic growth, Gilchrist ruled nothing out.

"That will give us a major programme of expansion in life assurance and general insurance as well," he said. "We'll look at the best (expansion) method. In some cases, organic growth from a solid base can be the best way."
He added that in other areas, where the Halifax has less experience, an acquisition might be indicated.
"We'll be cautious and careful, we won't let the capital burn a hole in our pockets."
Gilchrist said the Halifax was not interested in moving into the corporate lending area.
